questions.correctFeedback: Right — add the Y = 1 cells over X: 0.3 + 0.2 = 0.5.
questions.incorrectFeedback: A marginal adds the other variable out: P(Y = 1) = 0.3 + 0.2 = 0.5.

questions.stem: Same table. What is P(Y = 1 | X = 1)?
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — the X = 1 row is 0.1, 0.3, total 0.4; rescaled, 0.3/0.4 = 0.75.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Slice the X = 1 row (0.1 and 0.3, total 0.4) and rescale: 0.3/0.4 = 0.75.

questions.stem: f(x, y) = 4xy on the unit square. Are X and Y independent?
questions.correctFeedback: Correct — rectangular support and f = (2x)(2y), each a density on (0, 1).
questions.incorrectFeedback: The support is a rectangle and f(x, y) = (2x)(2y), a product of a function of x and a function of y. So yes, independent.

questions.stem: From Lesson 3: P(A) = 0.01, P(+ | A) = 0.9, P(+ | not A) = 0.1. P(A | +) is closest to…
questions.correctFeedback: Right — 0.009/(0.009 + 0.099) ≈ 0.083. False positives from the large not-A group swamp the true ones.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Bayes: P(A | +) = 0.009/(0.009 + 0.099) ≈ 0.083, not 0.9. The rare condition's true positives are outnumbered.

questions.stem: (X, Y) is uniform on the triangle 0 < x < y < 1. Are X and Y independent?
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — learning X = x forces Y > x, so the slices differ.
questions.incorrectFeedback: A constant density on a triangle is not a product: once X = x is known, Y must exceed x. Non-rectangular support rules independence out.
